conviction_note: Mostly offsetting evidence. The one company-document item is that Zacks' Oct-15 Consumer Products consensus (+8.2%) sits above the CFO's July Q3 phasing (+low single digits). Against it: a conservative FY guide that implies roughly flat H2, and the 8-of-8 beat record. A +13% run-up into the print and +6.6 put skew lean the reaction slightly negative. abs_move 8.5 (implied 8.39, median 8.14; this name trades on the FY guide: guide held May -8.8%, guide raised July +8.8%) times p_up 46 gives -0.68. The findings sum is -0.8, the same sign and size.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue consensus $1.47bn / adj EPS $1.86 (Zacks preview 2026-10-15, https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/stay-ahead-game-hasbro-q3-121520655.html). Benzinga has $1.48bn / $1.87, TickerLeague $1.50bn / $1.91 (9 analysts). Two sources agree within 1%. Company FY2026 guide: revenue +5-7% cc (about $4.94-5.03bn), adj op margin 25-26%, adj EBITDA $1.45-1.50bn (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000046080/000004608026000044/exhibit991q22026.htm). Q3 phasing from the Q2 call: Magic up mid-single digits, Consumer Products up low single digits (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-7-21-hasbro-inc-stock/).
positioning_check: Short interest about 5.2% of float with 2.5 days to cover (Equibles snapshot, 2026-08-19, https://equibles.com/stocks/HAS). Benzinga shows 5.8% short float around late September (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/HAS/sentiment), and MarketBeat 5.17% with 3.78 days, undated. Not a crowded short. Baseline: skew_25d +6.6 vol points (downside paid), put/call OI 0.49, run-up +13.42% over 20 sessions and +5.02% over 5, 6.1% below the 52-week high. Zacks Rank #4 (Sell), Q3 EPS revisions -0.1% over 30 days. Part of the run-up came after the WSJ's 2026-10-01 report of Authentic Brands takeover interest in Mattel (HAS +2% that day), and after Citi raised its target to $117 on 10-13.

findings.finding: Zacks' Q3 consensus (2026-10-15) has Consumer Products revenue at $862.3m, +8.2% y/y on about $797m. The CFO's Q2 call guided Q3 Consumer Products up low single digits (about $805-820m), so the consensus is about $40-55m (5-7% of the segment) above the company's own phasing. The Wizards consensus ($601.3m, +5.1%; tabletop +7.1%) is in line with the guided Magic +MSD. Built bottom-up from the company's phasing, Q3 revenue is about $1.43-1.45bn against the $1.47bn headline consensus, a gap of roughly 1.5-2.5%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Hasbro beat revenue in Q3 2025 ($1.39bn vs $1.35bn, stock +3.7%) and in Q2 2026 (stock +8.8%, on a guide raise). Q1 2026 beat EPS widely ($1.47 vs $1.13) but held the guide, and the stock fell 8.8%. Reported-quarter beats on their own have not set the sign; the guide has.
findings.why_not_priced: Headline consensus is set well above the company's own Q3 phasing for Consumer Products; if the street had marked down to the CFO's numbers, the segment estimate would sit near +2%, not +8%. The headline previews do not net the segment estimate against the call phasing. Counterweight: Q3 2025 Consumer Products was an easy compare (-7.3% on late retailer shelf resets), about $25m of cyber-lost Q2 revenue is to be recouped in H2, and toy prices are up 6.6% y/y. The company may simply beat its conservative phasing, as it has 8 of 8 times. That is why this is only -1.
findings.independence: Company phasing: https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-7-21-hasbro-inc-stock/ (Q2 call, 2026-07-21). Year-ago segment base: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/46080/000004608025000164/has-20250928.htm. Both are different documents from the consensus page.

findings.finding: The FY2026 guide (+5-7% cc, about $4.94-5.03bn) against H1 2026 revenue of about $2.14bn (Q1 about $1.00bn, Q2 $1.14bn) implies H2 revenue of about $2.80-2.89bn, roughly -1% to +2% against H2 2025 (about $2.83bn). Q3 consensus is already +6%. Holding the guide would therefore imply a lower Q4 (the CFO already flagged Q4 Magic down low single digits and about $40m of Magic moving from Q4 2026 into Q1 2027). This name trades on the guide: held in May, -8.8%; raised in July, +8.8%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-05-20: guide held at the low end against a street at about 5%, stock -8.8% (https://www.bostonglobe.com/2026/05/20/business/hasbro-shares-tumble-sales-guidance-disappoints/). 2026-07-21: guide raised from 3-5% to 5-7%, stock +8.8%.
findings.why_not_priced: The arithmetic is public, but the stock is up 13% in 20 sessions near its 52-week high. That reads as a market leaning toward another raise. If a hold were priced, the run-up and the analyst target raises (Citi $117 on 10-13) would not sit beside each other. Two-sided: a Q3 beat flowed into the range would be a raise.
findings.independence: FY2025 base of $4.7bn: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260209085774/en/Hasbro-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Year-2025-Financial-Results/. Q4 phasing: https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-7-21-hasbro-inc-stock/ (that call transcript is shared with finding 1).

findings.finding: Magic is supply-constrained into the Q3 close. ICv2's retailer column (2026-09-21) says major distributors were 'out of almost all Magic product'. Reality Fracture Collector Boosters and Commander decks were partially delayed by a Panama drought in shipping, and bundles may arrive after release. Hobbit Play Boosters were delayed to some US distributors until early September and short into October. Any shipment that slipped past the 2026-09-27 quarter end moves Wizards revenue from Q3 into Q4.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Wizards drove the positive reactions in Q2 2026 (+27%) and Q4 2025 (Magic +141%). There is no prior instance of a supply-driven Wizards shortfall in the baseline window.
findings.why_not_priced: The Wizards consensus (+5.1%) sits at the guided mid-single-digit Magic rate with no visible haircut for shipping slippage. A trade-press retailer column is not in the sell-side previews. Size is small because a timing shift inside H2 does not change the FY guide, and management already called supply constraints easing into 2027-28.
findings.independence: https://mtgrocks.com/mtg-the-hobbit-play-booster-delay/ (2026-08-15, Hobbit delay to early September). The same ICv2 column also supports the demand finding below; the two are different readings (timing vs demand) of partly one source.

findings.finding: Demand for the H2 Magic slate is strong. Marvel Super Heroes was the fastest set to $300m, with day-one and month-one records. Hobbit Play Booster displays traded at about $197 pre-launch against the typical $120-130 for major sets, with local shops selling out of preorders. Distributors clear Magic product almost immediately (ICv2, 2026-09-21). That supports Wizards at or above the guided mid-single digits, and 'line of sight to growth in 2027'.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the Marvel records were on the Q2 call, and the stock has run. What is left is the secondary-market premium on the Q3 set, which is not in the consensus segment numbers (+5.1% Wizards). Revenue is constrained by supply rather than demand (see the previous finding), so the upside is capped. Sized small.
findings.independence: https://icv2.com/articles/news/view/62920/magic-the-gathering-marvel-super-heroes-passes-lord-rings (Marvel passes LOTR, company statements). A contrary view: Marvel Play Booster boxes at about $116, under release pricing three months in (https://draftsim.com/tag/mtg-marvel-price-drops/).

findings.finding: Industry backdrop for Consumer Products: Circana US toy dollar sales rose 17% in H1 2026 (units +12%, ASP +4%), the best first half in six years (Retail Dive, 2026-08-20). US toy prices rose 4.2% m/m in September (seasonally adjusted) and 6.6% y/y (Reuters syndication, 2026-10-15). Both support Consumer Products revenue at or above the low-single-digit guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Consumer Products revenue of +5% in Q2 2026 and +7% in Q4 2025 came alongside positive reactions. Q3 2025 Consumer Products -7% (retailer timing) still saw the stock up 3.7% on Wizards.
findings.why_not_priced: This is an industry proxy that the company has not confirmed for Q3. The Zacks Consumer Products estimate of +8% may already reflect it, which would make it priced. A company where this was unpriced would carry a Consumer Products estimate near the low-single-digit guide. It is the counterweight to finding 1, kept separately because the source is different.
findings.independence: https://www.fox6now.com/news/holiday-toy-prices-tariffs-war (2026-10-15, toy CPI). This is a proxy; the conflicting License Global H1 figure is +7%, not +17% (https://www.licenseglobal.com/toys-games/u-s-toy-industry-achieves-strongest-first-half-growth-in-six-years-circana).

findings.finding: Digital and Licensed Gaming consensus is $125.2m, -3.8% y/y. The 10-Q shows the line at $135.5m in Q2 2026, +16.7% y/y ($116.1m in Q2 2025). The CFO described Monopoly GO royalties as a stable $12-14m/month run-rate, even though the game's IAP fell 52% y/y. The estimate looks low against the latest reported run-rate.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Licensed digital grew +21% in Q3 2025, inside a +3.7% reaction. It has not been the line the stock moves on.
findings.why_not_priced: The segment estimate is lower than the run-rate in the last 10-Q. If analysts had marked it to Q2, it would sit near flat to positive y/y. The amount is small (about $5-10m of high-margin revenue, about $0.03 EPS), hence +0.4.
findings.independence: https://naavik.co/digest/dissecting-scopelys-mobile-empire/ (2026-05-31: Monopoly GO royalties stable; game IAP down 52% y/y in April 2026). Consensus figure from the same Zacks page as finding 1.

findings.finding: Hasbro's Q2 10-Q says it made its first CBP application in Q3 2026 for a refund of 'a majority of the IEEPA tariffs' it paid, with more applications to follow, and that the amounts 'could affect its 2026 results'. A refund receivable or gain could appear in the Q3 GAAP results or cash flow.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior refund on this name. In the repo's experience, tariff-refund one-offs on other names split by the direction of guidance.
findings.why_not_priced: The amount is undisclosed, and Hasbro has never quantified the IEEPA duties it paid, so no estimate carries it. It is a one-off that will probably be excluded from adjusted results. Its only path to the multiple is cash for debt paydown or buybacks. Sized at a fraction.

findings.finding: The US and China agreed in late September 2026 to cut tariffs on about $30bn of goods each way, and the US list explicitly includes toys. Most of Hasbro's Consumer Products sourcing is Chinese, so this is a margin tailwind for Q4 2026 and 2027 that could firm the 25-26% adj operating margin guide or the 2027 commentary.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Tariff news has moved toy names on the guide. The 2026-07-21 margin guide raise (24-25% to 25-26%) came with +8.8%.
findings.why_not_priced: The cuts take effect only after domestic procedures, and the company has not commented on them. The news is public, though, and possibly part of the October run. A proxy, sized small.
findings.independence: https://www.fox6now.com/news/holiday-toy-prices-tariffs-war (2026-10-15: toymakers say prices set under higher tariffs are still reaching shelves, so the benefit comes later).

findings.finding: Input costs from the Iran war: in May Hasbro flagged a $30m 2026 impact from rising oil. On 2026-10-15 Fitch's David Silverman said the conflict's effect on commodity and shipping costs will persist 'for the next several quarters', and Mattel's CFO cited 'moderate inflationary pressures associated with events in the Middle East'. That is a risk to the Consumer Products margin (guided 6-8%) and to the Q4 commentary.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The $30m oil impact disclosed with Q1 (2026-05-20) came on a -8.8% day, alongside the held guide.
findings.why_not_priced: Already in the July guide raise to a 25-26% margin, which was made with oil costs known. Incremental only if costs rose further in Q3. A proxy from a peer and a rating agency, sized small.
findings.independence: Oil impact from Q1: https://www.bostonglobe.com/2026/05/20/business/hasbro-shares-tumble-sales-guidance-disappoints/. Shares a source with the toy CPI part of finding 5.

findings.finding: Positioning into the print: +13.4% over 20 sessions and +5.0% over 5, 6.1% below the 52-week high. The October leg started with the 2026-10-01 WSJ report of Authentic Brands takeover interest in Mattel (HAS +2% to $89.70 that day; closes $87.68 on 9-30 and $98.76 on 10-16). Put skew is +6.6 vol points, Zacks Rank is #4 (Sell), and 30-day EPS revisions are -0.1%. Part of the run is sector M&A read-across rather than estimate upgrades.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Into Q1 2026 the stock had not run in the same way and still fell 8.8% when the guide was held. There is no clean prior example of a 13% run into a Hasbro print in the baseline window.
findings.why_not_priced: The skew already says downside is paid, so this agrees with the option market rather than beating it. What is not priced: if the run is M&A-sympathy beta, it has no earnings support and is exposed to a merely in-line print. Short interest of about 5% is not crowded, so there is no squeeze offset.
findings.independence: Price path: https://www.investing.com/equities/hasbro-inc-historical-data. Citi target to $117 on 2026-10-13: https://www.ad-hoc-news.de/boerse/news/nebenwerte/citi-lifts-target-for-hasbro-stock-to-usd-117-00/70351530 (a positive driver of the same run).

findings.finding: Cyber incident: about $25m of Q2 revenue was lost (against an earlier assumed $40-60m), and the company said it would be recouped in the back half. The 10-Q says no insurance proceeds had yet been recognized and that 'a less significant amount of additional costs' is expected. A Q3 insurance recovery or the revenue catch-up could appear in the quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The cyber update was part of the -8.8% Q1 reaction. It was a non-issue at Q2 (+8.8%).
findings.why_not_priced: Insurance recovery is excluded from adjusted results, and the revenue recoup sits inside the company's H2 Consumer Products guide. Mostly priced, so near zero.

findings.finding: Wizards of the Coast president John Hight stepped down on 2026-09-01 (8-K Item 5.02, 2026-07-27). With no successor named in the coverage found, Wizards reports to CEO Cocks on an interim basis. A successor announcement or 2027 slate commentary could come with the print.
findings.why_not_priced: Public since July. The stock rose through it, so it is priced and sized at 0.

outside_window.finding: Mattel moved its Q3 2026 report to 2026-11-05 (later than its usual late-October slot) while takeover interest from Authentic Brands is reported. The peer read-across and any deal news land after the HAS window.
The Star Trek Universes Beyond set (November 2026) and the Q1 2027 Magic release timing ($40m shifting from Q4 into Q1) fall outside the window, apart from any guide commentary.

searched_and_found_nothing: A September or October 2026 investor conference with Hasbro management remarks: none found
Monopoly GO monthly revenue for July-September 2026 (Sensor Tower): latest found is April 2026
Circana Q3 or September YTD 2026 US toy data: not found, only H1
Short interest settlement for 2026-09-30: not found, latest dated is the 2026-08-19 Equibles snapshot
Hasbro 8-Ks after 2026-07-27: EDGAR shows none (browse-edgar list for CIK 46080)
Wizards of the Coast president successor: none named in coverage found
Wells Fargo August 2026 downgrade rationale: could not be confirmed beyond the Benzinga listing

rejected_candidates.candidate: Report of Mattel takeover interest from Hasbro in 2026
rejected_candidates.detail: The Hasbro-Mattel approach stories are from 2017. The October 2026 WSJ story names Authentic Brands as the suitor (Reuters/Investing.com, 2026-10-01). It is used only as positioning context in finding 10.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Marvel Super Heroes Play Booster boxes trading at about $116, below release pricing, read as Magic oversupply
rejected_candidates.detail: Merged into finding 4's independence as the contrary datapoint. It is weak: the 'MSRP' comparison multiplies the per-pack price by 30, and Marvel revenue was largely shipped in Q2.
The company's Q2 release gives no tariff dollar figure; it says only 'incremental tariff expense'. The secondary figure cannot be verified against the 8-K.

baseline_tension: The net lean agrees with the +6.6 put skew and fades the +13% run-up, so it is largely what the option market already says. Against it, Hasbro has beaten 8 of 8 quarters, its FY guide is conservative, and Magic demand is strong. That is why p_up sits only 4 points below 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 5 (proxy smaller than a primary document): toy-industry Circana/CPI finding cut from +0.5 to +0.4, Iran/oil cost finding cut from -0.3 to -0.2. Both are kept as proxies.
Rule 2 (one-offs at a fraction): IEEPA refund application cut from +0.3 to +0.2, cyber insurance/recoup cut from +0.2 to +0.1.

Rule 6 (verify the bar): the bar is sourced to Zacks plus Benzinga, agreeing within 1%, so it is not capped. Finding 1 rests on the company's own call phasing (a primary document), so it stays at -1.0.
Rule 7 (positioning): short interest of about 5% is not crowded, so the negatives are not shrunk for squeeze risk. The skew agrees with the negative lean, so p_up moves to 46 rather than further.
Rule 9 (segment net of the rest): Consumer Products finding 1 checked against Wizards. The Wizards consensus matches the guided Magic +MSD, so there is no offset larger than findings 4 and 6.
Rule 1 (fact vs reaction): the reaction runs on the FY guide (May -8.8%, July +8.8%), so abs_move is kept at 8.5 and the uncertainty goes into p_up (46), not into the sizes.
